claims.exact_statement: For every Boolean g on n sign coordinates, its parity lift F(x,z)=g(x_1z,...,x_nz) has Fourier coefficient ghat(S) at lambda(S)=S for even |S| and S union {z} for odd |S|, hence H(F)=H(g), I(F)=I(g)+Pr(|S| odd)<=2I(g), and only even Fourier degrees occur. Nevertheless, for every r>=3 the parity lift of the parity-shifted one-point defect has positive normalized degree-damped spectral-entropy derivative at t=0. Therefore even Fourier support does not restore monotone entropy dissipation, and a bound V_-(F)<=C I(F) on the parity-lift class alone implies full FEI with constant 2C. Parity-lifted addressing and unshifted one-point defects satisfy V_-=H and V_-/I<4.
